title: Execute Trace Harness Against Available Evidence
execution_mode: static_source_trace_against_MBBSEmu_GitHub_source; no live Classic runtime or instrumented MBBSEmu process executed
canonical_rule: Librarium remains canonical. MBBSEmu observations are evidence only.

observations.name: Scheduler Cadence Probe
observations.conclusion: MBBSEmu uses a Timer.Hertz gate when idle; default Timer.Hertz resolves to 36 if unset/invalid. WaitForNextTick returns immediately when sessions have pending inbound/outbound/process data, so busy conditions are event-driven rather than purely fixed-frequency.
evidence: MBBSEmu/HostProcess/MbbsHost.cs: WaitForNextTick returns if DataFromClient/DataToClient/DataToProcess is pending

observations.name: Callback Registration Probe
observations.conclusion: Host-visible callback surfaces are confirmed in MBBSEmu: STTROU, STSROU, BEGIN_POLLING, RTKICK, RTIHDLR, SYSCYC, INITASK. Which of these the original MajorMUD module registers still requires module-specific trace or binary evidence.
evidence: MBBSEmu/HostProcess/ExportedModules/Ordinals.cs ordinals include BEGIN_POLLING, RTIHDLR, RTKICK, SYSCYC

observations.name: Timed Callback Ordering Probe
observations.conclusion: In the MBBSEmu worker loop, per-session processing completes before timed/real-time events. After sessions are processed, host order is ProcessRTKICK, then ProcessRTIHDLR, then ProcessSYSCYC, then ProcessTasks. RTIHDLR itself is gated to roughly 55ms elapsed.
evidence: MBBSEmu/HostProcess/MbbsHost.cs WorkerThread calls ProcessRTKICK(); ProcessRTIHDLR(); ProcessSYSCYC(); ProcessTasks(); in that order

observations.name: Output Flush Ordering Probe
observations.conclusion: Output is enqueued with SendToClient/DataToClient from host/module services. Worker wake-up considers DataToClient pending, so outbound data can drive additional processing. Exact socket flush order relative to every module state update needs live trace instrumentation.
evidence: MBBSEmu source shows many ChannelDictionary[channel].SendToClient(...) call sites

observations.name: World Iteration Probe
observations.conclusion: The host iterates sessions serially in _channelDictionary.Values, processing input, GSBL events, module entry/login/in-module callbacks, status routines, STTROU, and polling before timed events. Internal MajorMUD ordering of NPCs, rooms, combat, regen, quests, and spawns is not proven by host source alone.
evidence: MBBSEmu/HostProcess/MbbsHost.cs session states EnteringModule/LoginRoutines/InModule and polling routine path
